explanation: All numbers of the RAW comparative LCA live in this workbook. The model reads it (via a snapshot saved in the code repository), so every value you enter is used in the results. Nothing is hidden in the code.

Tabs are grouped and ordered by their role in the LCA; each group has its own colour (tab, header row and cells). The lci_raw_* tabs are filled in by the case partners; all other tabs are maintained by the LCA team - please do not edit them, ask instead.
fu_comparison, study_setup, impact_categories, scenarios
lci_raw_biopol, lci_raw_timber, lci_raw_cfw, lci_raw_knit, lci_baselines
product_size_formulas, product_size_constants
unit_burdens_dataSources, benefits_constants_dataSources, EoL_constants, eol_routes
constants, gwpbio_table, dcf_bern

One row per RAW case: its functional unit (name, function, service life over which it is compared with its baselines), its quantifier (e.g. beam span in m), and the baseline products (conventional bio-based / conventional fossil-based) it is compared with.

lci_raw_biopol, lci_raw_timber, lci_raw_cfw, lci_raw_knit: one row = one number of your prototype. Fill in `typical`, `min`, `max`, `source` and set `status` for every row. Fill `scaled_up` only for production steps that should use different values at large scale (see 'Scaling up a machine' below).

lci_baselines: one row = one input or output per kg of product. production rows: materials and other inputs (item = an activity on unit_burdens_dataSources). end-of-life rows: item = the waste treatment (an activity on unit_burdens_dataSources with an eol_type), qualifier = the material that is treated (a row of EoL_constants, which gives its allocation factor, quality ratio and heating value for the circular footprint formula). The product_size_formulas tab gives the kg of product.

(lci_raw_* tabs only) design = what the product is made of; manufacturing = machines, loading, yield; circularity = lifetime, repair, end of life; location = which country's electricity. The groups are used in the sensitivity analysis, which covers the RAW cases only.

typical = your best estimate. min and max = how low / high it could realistically be. If a number is fixed, set min = max = typical. Rows with missing min/max are highlighted in red; they are treated as fixed.
triangular (typical is the most likely value), uniform, fixed, or choice (for text values such as a country code or virgin/recycled).
source = where the number comes from (measurement, colleague, paper, datasheet). status: placeholder (first guess by the LCA team, highlighted yellow), partner estimate, measured, literature.

stage = production, repair, use, end-of-life, or general (the location row). item = the material, the process step or 'waste' the number belongs to. The order of process steps is the order of the rows.
Bill-of-materials shares and end-of-life shares of one stage should add up to 100 %. The model re-normalises them.
Share of the material entering a step that leaves it as good output (the rest becomes waste). Output rate = kg processed per hour. Machine lifetime = operating hours.

The number of repair events is not entered: it is the smallest number of repairs that makes the product last the service life of its functional unit (fu_comparison), i.e. (service life - expected lifetime) / lifetime extension per repair, rounded up, and 0 if the expected lifetime already reaches it.

A production step is scaled up if its `scaled_up` cells are filled in (machine weight, power, output rate, machine lifetime, all four); the model uses those values instead of the prototype ones for that step in the 'scaled up' variant. Leave `scaled_up` blank to keep the step at prototype scale.

Do not rename tabs or columns, and do not delete rows without asking: the model reads them by name. You may add rows: copy a row of the same kind and change `item` (a new material must exist on tab unit_burdens_dataSources).
